title: Momentum and Impulse
unit: IAL Mechanics (M1) (unit inferred from file name)

questions.question: Particle P has mass km and particle Q has mass m. They move towards each other along the same line and collide directly. Immediately before, P has speed 3u and Q has speed u. After the collision each direction of motion is reversed and each speed is halved. Find the value of k.
steps: Take P's initial direction as positive: before, P has +3u and Q has -u
After: P has -3u/2 and Q has +u/2
Conservation of momentum: km(3u) + m(-u) = km(-3u/2) + m(u/2)
Divide by mu: 3k - 1 = -3k/2 + 1/2

questions.question: Find, in terms of m and u, the magnitude of the impulse exerted on Q in the collision.
steps: Impulse on Q = change in momentum of Q
Q changes from -u to +u/2, a change of 3u/2 in velocity
Impulse = m(3u/2) = 3mu/2 N s
Check: impulse on P = (m/3)(-3u/2 - 3u) = -3mu/2, equal and opposite

questions.question: Particle P of mass 3m and particle Q of mass 5m move towards each other along the same line on a smooth horizontal surface and collide directly. Before the collision P has speed ku and Q has speed 2u. After the collision P has speed u and Q has speed 3u, with the direction of Q reversed. Find, in terms of m and u, the magnitude of the impulse exerted on Q by P.
steps: Take P's initial direction as positive: Q before has velocity -2u
Q after has velocity +3u (direction reversed)
Impulse on Q = 5m(3u - (-2u)) = 5m(5u)
Magnitude = 25mu N s

questions.question: Find the two possible values of k.
steps: Let v be the velocity of P after the collision: 3m(ku) + 5m(-2u) = 3mv + 5m(3u)
3ku - 10u = 3v + 15u, so v = ku - 25u/3
P has speed u after the collision, so v = u or v = -u
v = u gives ku = 28u/3, so k = 28/3
v = -u gives ku = 22u/3, so k = 22/3

questions.question: Particles P (mass 2m) and Q (mass m) move towards each other along the same line on a smooth horizontal plane and collide directly. Immediately before the collision P has speed 3u and Q has speed 2u. The magnitude of the impulse exerted on Q by P is 5mu. Find the speed of P immediately after the collision.
steps: Take P's initial direction as positive: P before +3u, Q before -2u
The impulse on Q acts in the direction of P's motion, so Q after = -2u + 5u = 3u
Conservation of momentum: 2m(3u) + m(-2u) = 2m v_P + m(3u)
4mu = 2m v_P + 3mu, so v_P = u/2
Speed of P immediately after = u/2

questions.question: Using the same collision as in part (a), find the speed of Q immediately after the collision.
steps: Impulse on Q = m(v_Q - (-2u)) = 5mu
v_Q + 2u = 5u, so v_Q = 3u
Speed of Q immediately after = 3u, moving in P's original direction

questions.question: Particles P and Q move towards each other in opposite directions along the same straight line and collide directly. Immediately before the collision the speed of Q is 2u. The mass of Q is 3m and the magnitude of the impulse exerted by P on Q is 4mu. Find the speed of Q immediately after the collision.
steps: Take P's initial direction as positive: Q before has velocity -2u
The impulse on Q acts in the direction of P's motion: 3m(v_Q + 2u) = 4mu
Speed of Q immediately after = 2u/3

questions.question: Find the direction of motion of Q immediately after the collision, using the collision in part (a).
questions.answer: Q continues in its original direction (not reversed)
steps: Velocity of Q after the collision is -2u/3
This is negative, the same sign as Q's velocity before the collision (-2u)
So Q carries on in its original direction of motion

questions.question: Railway truck S of mass 20 tonnes moves at 4 m/s along a straight horizontal track and collides with truck T of mass 30 tonnes which is at rest. The trucks join together. Find the common speed immediately after the collision.
steps: Conservation of momentum with 20 tonnes = 20000 kg: 20000 x 4 = (20000 + 30000)v

questions.question: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted on S in the collision, stating the units of your answer.
steps: Impulse on S = change in its momentum = 20000(1.6 - 4)
Magnitude = 48000 N s (equivalently kg m/s)

questions.question: Particle P of mass 2m moves on a rough horizontal plane with speed 3u and collides directly with particle Q of mass 4m at rest. Immediately after the collision Q has speed 2u. Find, in terms of u, the speed of P immediately after the collision.
steps: Take P's initial direction as positive: P before +3u, Q before 0
Conservation of momentum: 2m(3u) = 2m v_P + 4m(2u)
6mu = 2m v_P + 8mu, so 2m v_P = -2mu
v_P = -u, so the speed of P after the collision is u

questions.question: State clearly the direction of motion of P immediately after the collision.
questions.answer: P reverses, moving in the opposite direction to its original motion
steps: Velocity of P after the collision is -u
The negative sign is opposite to P's original positive direction
So P moves back the way it came

questions.question: Following the collision, particle Q (mass 4m, speed 2u) comes to rest after travelling a distance 6u^2/g along the rough plane. The coefficient of friction between Q and the plane is mu. Find the value of mu.
steps: Friction on Q = mu(4mg), so deceleration = mu g
Using v^2 = u^2 - 2as with initial speed 2u, final speed 0 and s = 6u^2/g

questions.topic: Common Speed Of Hammer And Peg
questions.question: A hammer of mass 1.8 kg is moving vertically downwards at 10 m/s and strikes a tent peg of mass 0.2 kg which is stationary. Immediately after the impact the hammer and peg move together vertically downwards with the same speed v m/s. Find the value of v.
steps: The impact is a direct collision, so momentum is conserved
v = 9 m/s

questions.question: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted on the tent peg by the hammer, stating the units of your answer.
steps: Impulse on peg = change in momentum of peg
Impulse = 1.8 N s (kg m/s)

questions.question: The ground exerts a constant vertical resistive force of magnitude R N, bringing the hammer and tent peg to rest after they travel a distance of 12 cm. Find the value of R.
steps: Deceleration a: v^2 = 2as, so 9^2 = 2a(0.12), giving a = 337.5 m/s^2
Forces on the combined 2 kg mass: R upwards and weight 2g downwards
Newton's second law (upwards positive): R - 2g = 2 x 337.5

questions.question: Particle A (mass 4 kg) and particle B (mass 2 kg) move towards each other along the same line on a smooth horizontal table and collide directly. Immediately before, A has speed 2u m/s and B has speed 3u m/s. Immediately after, B has speed 2u m/s and its direction is reversed. Find, in terms of u, the speed of A immediately after the collision.
steps: Take A's initial direction as positive: A before +2u, B before -3u
B after: +2u (direction reversed)
Conservation of momentum: 4(2u) + 2(-3u) = 4v_A + 2(2u)
2u = 4v_A + 4u, so v_A = -u/2
Speed of A immediately after = u/2

questions.question: State the direction of motion of A immediately after the collision.
questions.answer: A reverses: it moves in the opposite direction to its original motion
steps: Velocity of A after the collision is -u/2
The negative sign is opposite to A's original direction
So A moves back the way it came, in the same direction as B's original motion

questions.question: Find, in terms of u, the magnitude of the impulse received by B in the collision. State the units of your answer.
steps: B before: -3u; B after: +2u
Change in B's momentum = 2(2u - (-3u)) = 2(5u) = 10u
Impulse magnitude = 10u N s (kg m/s)

questions.question: Block A of mass 9 kg is released from rest at point P, a height h m above horizontal soft ground. It falls and strikes block B (mass 1.5 kg) which is on the ground vertically below P. The speed of A immediately before it strikes B is 7 m/s. Both blocks are modelled as particles. Find h.
steps: A falls freely from rest: v^2 = 2gh

questions.question: Immediately after the impact the blocks move downwards together with the same speed and both come to rest after sinking a vertical distance of 12 cm into the ground. The ground's resistance has constant magnitude R N. Find the value of R.
steps: Momentum in the impact: 9(7) = (9 + 1.5)v, so v = 6 m/s
Deceleration: 6^2 = 2a(0.12), so a = 150 m/s^2 (upwards)
Combined mass 10.5 kg: weight 10.5g downwards, resistance R upwards

questions.question: Particles A (mass 3m) and B (mass m) move in a straight line towards each other on a smooth horizontal surface, each with speed 1.5 m/s before colliding directly. After the collision A's direction is unchanged and the difference between the speed of A and the speed of B is 1 m/s. Find (i) the speed of A immediately after the collision, (ii) the speed of B immediately after the collision.
steps: Take A's initial direction as positive: A before +1.5, B before -1.5
Let A's speed after be a (a > 0), and B's velocity after be v_B
Conservation of momentum: 3m(1.5) + m(-1.5) = 3ma + m v_B, so 3 = 3a + v_B
With B rebounding (v_B = +s) and s - a = 1: 3 = 3a + (a + 1), so a = 1/2 and s = 3/2
Note: a = 1 m/s with B at rest also fits the wording; the intended answer takes B to rebound

questions.topic: Impulse On B In Terms Of m
questions.question: Find, in terms of m, the magnitude of the impulse exerted on B in the collision.
steps: B before: -1.5; B after: +1.5 (from part a)
Impulse on B = m(1.5 - (-1.5)) = 3m
Magnitude = 3m N s

questions.question: Particles P (mass m) and Q (mass km) move in opposite directions along the same horizontal straight line and collide directly. Immediately before the collision P has speed u and Q has speed 2u. As a result, the direction of motion of each particle is reversed and each speed is halved. Find the value of k.
steps: Take P's initial direction as positive: P before +u, Q before -2u
After: P has -u/2 and Q has +u
Conservation of momentum: m(u) + km(-2u) = m(-u/2) + km(u)
Divide by mu: 1 - 2k = -1/2 + k, so 3/2 = 3k

keywords: in terms of m and u
questions.question: Find, in terms of m and u only, the magnitude of the impulse exerted on Q by P in the collision.
steps: Q before -2u; Q after +u
Change in Q's momentum = (m/2)(u - (-2u)) = (m/2)(3u)
Impulse magnitude = 3mu/2 N s
